newsitem.title: MEXICO: Serfin's Sada sees sale this week.
newsitem.headline: Serfin's Sada sees sale this week.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Serfin SA de CV Chairman Adrian Sada said on Tuesday he expected the banking group to announce the sale of 19.9 percent of its stock this week.
The most highly expected suitor is London-based HSBC Holdings Plc, holding company for Hongkong and Shanghai Bank. Sada was asked when the sale "to the Asian bank" would be announced.
"We're on the point of closing the deal; I think we'll announce it in two more days. At the moment I can give no more details," he told reporters.

Sada was attending the inauguration of a new plant run by Vitro SA, parent of Serfin. At the event, members of Midland Hong Kong Shanghai Bank, a unit of HSBC, milled around, identified by their nametags.

Sada said the sale would pay off a $280 million bridge loan extended to Serfin last year by J.P. Morgan & Co Inc. Serfin needs to create 1.24 billion pesos of fresh capital this year as part of a commitment to bank insurance fund Fobaproa, which last year bought billions of pesos of bad loans from the bank, one of the most stricken in the banking system.

Banca Serfin announced on Tuesday the sale of another 10.3 billion pesos of mortgage loans to Fobaproa. It also unveiled a net loss of 7.446 billion in 1996, partly as a result of strong provisioning for loan losses.
